questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: On a vehicle with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, you should watch the road about ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to spot dangers early. At highway speeds, this equals about a quarter mile.

questions.question: How must a shipper notify a driver of the risks associated with their cargo?

options.text: By writing a note on a blank piece of paper
By putting hazard warning labels on packages
By placing orange dots on packages

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages
questions.explanation: Shippers must use proper shipping papers, hazard warning labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards to alert drivers and others to hazards.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: In addition to reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual covers what you need to pass the test, but it is just the first step. Take hazardous materials training courses to learn more about federal and state rules.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials correctly. Drivers should verify that materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: Unbaffled tanks are also referred to as ____ tanks.
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks are also called smooth bore tanks.

questions.question: Placards showing the type of hazardous materials in a vehicle are usually shaped like what?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts suggests they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight before you start driving.

questions.question: Unless the package is clearly unsafe, a driver needs ____ to accept a package.
questions.explanation: Shippers certify that hazardous materials have been packaged correctly. Unless a package is clearly unsafe or does not follow regulations, you can accept the shipper's certification.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think there is a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic around you and watch for problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: What information does a hazardous materials shipping paper show?

options.text: How the materials will be transported

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are examples of shipping papers.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle turns a corner?

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels go over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is more noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: Which item is not required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher. A loud horn is not required.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Prevent the wheels from locking up
Alert other drivers when you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: When it is hard to see (at dawn or dusk), what is the best way to make your vehicle visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (at dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights. Do not use high beams when driving near other vehicles.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is set to "emergency"?
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, the tractor protection control may use a lever. When set to "emergency", the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: When using controlled braking with liquid cargo, how should you apply the brakes?

options.text: Gently to keep the wheels rolling.
As hard as it takes to lock up the wheels.
As hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: As hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: With controlled braking, apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Make small steering wheel movements when braking this way.

questions.question: What is acceptable to find during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Check that your tires have at least 4/32 inch tread depth on front tires and 2/32 inch on other tires. Make sure tires are not cracked, have proper air pressure, and are all the same size. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop your vehicle within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area you can see. Slow down whenever you cannot see far enough ahead to stop safely.
